display_title: runtime: recover only orchestration-blocked zero-delta repairs
summary: FIRST FIRING OF THE NEW NARROW RF-X RECOVERY — the external orchestration decision demanded by the Runtime audit chain was converted into a same-cycle repair dispatch. Self-referential wake: the trigger commit 5e63927 (+34/-2 on runtime-supervisor.yml) ADDED exactly the recovery block this firing then executed. Executed logic (curator-read from the log, byte-durable at the pinned commit): read CYCLE_<latest>_RUNTIME_GATE.json from cycle/runtime/<id>/audit; gate conditions GATE==BLOCKED && delta_since_prior_audit_bytes==0 && RF-X external_decision_required>0; verify launcher fix ZERO_DELTA_LAUNCHER_FIX=751496ad505c0f6cc9c54272c517e41c0d243dc4 ('infra: fail zero-delta repairs and pin retry cwd', 18:40:18Z) reachable on main; then emit '::warning::Runtime BLOCKED only on RF-X zero-delta orchestration. Launcher fix is present; dispatching one same-cycle recovery repair round 3.' and dispatch runtime-loop with repair_from_run_id + repair_round=3 (curator-inferred target: the r2 gate of run 32877702179, whose audit fired BLOCKED/RF-X and which watchdog #81 had just seen as runtime-loop's latest completed run). The dispatched human_note freezes orchestration files ('Do not attempt to edit workflow/orchestration files'), demands substantive RF1-RF6 'from the mounted audit', and requires preserving 'the frozen R0 benchmark and all audit constraints' (cycle_index=1, max_cycles=0). Context embedded in-script: repeated byte-identical repairs were caused by a retry returning rc=0 with zero durable delta; the shared launcher now pins cwd and rejects zero-delta REPAIR success.

findings.summary: RF-X closure mechanism worked as designed end-to-end: an EXTERNAL/ORCHESTRATION decision (the only kind RF-X accepted) was delivered as the 751496a+5e63927 commit pair, machine-verified by the supervisor (fix commit reachable), and converted into exactly ONE bounded same-cycle repair round 3 with anti-gaming constraints in the human_note. This is the productive continuation path the Runtime record chain anticipated after BLOCKED.

Whether round 3 finally produces nonzero delta is OPEN — successor run 32885208777 exists server-side but has no local bundle or record yet. If it repeats zero-delta, the current ladder has no terminal rule beyond rounds; the escalation design should be revisited before another round is spent.

Self-referential trigger pattern observed again (cf. council feed-gate deaths): the commit adding a recovery capability also triggers its first real firing. Here it was PRODUCTIVE (recovery executed immediately) — contrast cto-council.yml where self-trigger pushes only produced queued deaths; the difference is supervisor workflows are cheap/fast while the council occupies a long single-slot group.
